1. Meaning of National Renaissance

  • National Renaissance refers to the intellectual, social, religious and cultural awakening that developed in India mainly during the nineteenth century.
  • It challenged:
  • Social evils.
  • Caste discrimination.
  • Gender inequality.
  • Religious superstition.
  • Educational backwardness.
  • It also contributed to the emergence of modern Indian nationalism.
📌 Must-Memorise

National Renaissance → Social Reform + Religious Reform + Modern Education + National Awakening

2. Background of the Renaissance

  • Major causes included:
  • Western education.
  • Printing press.
  • Growth of newspapers.
  • Christian missionary criticism.
  • Rediscovery of India's past.
  • New middle classes.
  • Social reform movements.
  • Colonial rule.

3. Role of Western Education

  • Western education introduced Indians to ideas such as:
  • Liberty.
  • Equality.
  • Rationalism.
  • Human rights.
  • Scientific inquiry.
  • Constitutional government.

4. Role of English

  • English became an important medium through which educated Indians accessed European political and philosophical thought.
  • It also allowed educated Indians from different regions to communicate with one another.

5. Printing Press and Reform

  • Printing helped spread:
  • Newspapers.
  • Pamphlets.
  • Reform literature.
  • Religious debates.
  • Political criticism.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Print Culture → Social Reform + Public Opinion

  • Clerks.
  • Doctors.
  • Government employees.
  • This class played a major role in reform and nationalism.

  • Orientalist scholars and Indian intellectuals studied:
  • Sanskrit.
  • Persian.
  • Ancient inscriptions.
  • Religious texts.
  • Classical literature.
  • This contributed to new pride in India's historical achievements.
